newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in UK firmer on dollar strength.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in UK firmer on dollar strength.

text.p: Japanese stocks in London were modestly firmer on Tuesday amid continued yen weakness against the dollar, traders said.
Interest was seen mostly in the blue-chip electronics stocks and exporters which are perceived to benefit from dollar strength, but volume was thin.

"Most of the business today is one way with the dollar/yen appreciating above 126 and that's good news for exporters, so everybody is trying to pick up as many of these names as they possibly can," one trader said.
The dollar was trading at 126.30 yen by 1420 GMT.
Traders said some of the weaker sectors in Tokyo over the last few days, such as banks and securities companies, were starting to attract bargain-hunters.

"Generally things look very good for the index as most of the sectors that have been holding it back are seeing bargain-hunters and the issues that have been driving it higher are seeing continued buying," another trader said.
Sony Corp was 20 yen higher in London at 9,140 from its Tokyo close while Sharp was also up 20 yen at 1,520.
In Tokyo on Tuesday the 225-share Nikkei average rose 306.03 points, or 1.73 percent to end at 18,021.70, inspired by the yen's weakness against the dollar, brokers said.
